To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of alkali metal mediated metalation (AMM) and N-hetereocyclic carbene chemistry allows for a novel C-N activation and ring opening process, which is triggered by lateral alkali metal metalation.
the C-N bond activation of saturated NHCs by alkali metals proceeds via lateral metalation of carbene and the resulting metalated carbene is prone to ring-opening reactions.
the C-N bond in a saturated NHC can be activated by lateral metalation with an alkali metal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the synthesis of organic compounds, the understanding of the underlying reaction mechanisms, and the design of new catalytic systems for organic transformations.
the development of novel synthetic methods for the preparation of organometallic compounds and the investigation of the mechanisms involved.
the synthesis of new organometallic complexes and the development of new reaction types.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the C-N bond of saturated NHCs can be cleaved by AMMM, which is a rare and unusual process for this type of ligand.
this process is initiated by a lateral metalation at the carbene carbon, followed by a C-H activation and a subsequent N-C bond cleavage, which is facilitated by a transmetalation process.
the alkali-metal-mediated ring-opening process is a two-step process, involving a lateral metalation of one of the carbene NHCs followed by a subsequent C-N bond activation of the other NHC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the alkali metal is the key to the ring-opening reaction of N-heterocycle carbene.
the NHC SIMes can undergo lateral metalation by alkali-metal reagents, and that this metalation is a key step in the C-N bond activation of the NHC.

alkali-metal-mediated lateral metalation of a saturated NHC leads to a transient metal-acyl species which can undergo C-N bond activation, and that this is a fundamentally different process from that observed for the corresponding unsaturated NHC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NHC ring-opening process is a consequence of the metalation of the NHC backbone and not of the NHC ring itself, as previously proposed.
the AMMM approach can be used to activate C-N bonds in NHC molecules and, by extension, other robust N-donor ligands, and thus to open up new synthetic avenues for these molecules.
alkali metals are capable of activating saturated NHCs, which are generally thought to be resistant to nucleophilic attack.
